clue.text: Standard work of Mensa not likely to be taken on board

definitions.text: not likely to be taken on board

parts.note: par is the standard score in golf

indicators.note: to work something is to knead or rework it, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clever society's set text is too dull for anyone to accept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' rearranges MENSA into MESAN. The definition is cryptic: the board is a cheeseboard, where a hard grating cheese is seldom served.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard Italian grating cheese is kept for sprinkling on pasta rather than laid out on a cheeseboard after dinner.

clue.text: "Your fat friend" the, church, vaguely green in its publications?

clue.text: See 1
Steersman in starting point turns up with a missile

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the built word is read from bottom to top
the steersman sits inside the starting point

parts.note: a golf hole starts from the tee
a cox steers a rowing boat

explanation.surface: A helmsman at the start line suddenly arrives carrying a rocket.
explanation.walkthrough: COX goes inside TEE to make TECOXE, and 'turns up' reads that upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The French-built anti-ship guided weapon became famous in the Falklands War.

clue.text: Chatter in a need for fuel

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Chatter in a need for fuel': CHATTER IN A is anagram fodder for ANTHRACITE but 'need' cannot signal an anagram; the indicator word is misread by OCR and no source gives it.
annotationWithheld.clue: Chatter in a need for fuel

clue.text: Season for the rich Yale, for example

parts.note: spring is one of the four seasons
loaded is slang for very wealthy

explanation.surface: A term of the year is set aside for wealthy students at an Ivy League university.
explanation.walkthrough: Yale looks like the American university; it is the lock maker, whose cylinder locks have a catch pushed by a coil.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yale lock's latch is held in place by a coil that snaps it shut, a classic example of such a mechanism.

clue.text: Sort of wood for opening with a hoe

parts.note: ply is wood made of thin glued layers
a mouth is an opening

explanation.surface: Advice on which timber to use when starting work with a garden tool.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hoe is the famous seafront park of a Devon port city, so 'with a hoe' defines the place rather than a garden tool.
explanation.definitionFit: The Devon naval city is known for the Hoe, the open grassy headland where Drake supposedly played bowls.

clue.text: Setter's placed outside study for being cheeky

parts.note: the setter says I'm, short for I am

indicators.note: the word for placed goes around the word for study

parts.note: put means placed
a den is a private study

explanation.surface: A crossword compiler is sent out of the classroom for answering back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter's' gives I'M, the compiler speaking of themself, and 'outside' wraps PUT round DEN to make PUDENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone rude and disrespectful in a bold way.

clue.text: Problem with toenail from Worthing

indicators.note: the answer is made from the letters of the town name, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone from a seaside town complains of a foot ailment.
explanation.walkthrough: Worthing is a seaside town in Sussex; 'from' says its letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail growing into the flesh around it is the classic painful toenail complaint.

clue.text: Work of setter, one taking a short view?

parts.note: the setter's own, so my
op is short for opus, a work
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A compiler's creation is the product of someone who cannot see far.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work of setter' reads as MY OP, the setter speaking of their own opus.
explanation.definitionFit: Short sight means seeing near things clearly but distant things blurred.

clue.text: Capital is a possibility for the right artist

parts.note: can be means it is possible
an RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A capital city might be the perfect subject for the right painter.
explanation.definitionFit: The planned city in the Australian Capital Territory is the country's seat of government.

clue.text: See 5
Layabout, at no time poets- STONED BLOSSOM cal, meets ballet dancer A R E Q E

parts.note: ne'er is the poetic contraction of never, at no time
Sir Anthony Dowell was a principal dancer of the Royal Ballet

explanation.surface: An idler who never writes verse bumps into a ballerina.
explanation.walkthrough: Anthony Dowell was a celebrated British ballet dancer and director of the Royal Ballet.
explanation.definitionFit: A good-for-nothing who idles about is a classic loafer.

clue.text: Peccant (corrupt) insertion into card written with pleasure

indicators.note: the rearranged word is put inside the card

parts.note: an ace is a playing card

indicators.note: corrupted letters are scrambled into a new order

explanation.surface: A sinful note slipped into a greetings card is received gladly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupt' rearranges PECCANT into CCEPTAN, which 'insertion into' places inside ACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal reply to an invitation traditionally says one accepts with pleasure.

clue.text: Starters at public house: E H this is for consumption

indicators.note: the opening letters of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: At the pub, the first course is served for eating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starters at' takes the first letters of 'public house', PH, which also abbreviates the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Consumption is the old name for tuberculosis, a wasting lung disease.

clue.text: What beetles this time left A G R R R A for old youth leader

parts.note: a beetling brow is one that juts out
now means at this time

explanation.surface: Insects departing today were a scout master's concern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beetles' is a verb, to overhang, not insects. A Brown Owl leads a pack of Brownies, the junior Girl Guides.
explanation.definitionFit: The adult in charge of a Brownie pack is called by this title.

clue.text: Extra charged particle: a theologian takes it first

indicators.note: the theologian's group comes first, ahead of the charged particle

parts.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian
taken as written
an ion is an electrically charged atom

explanation.surface: An extra charged particle is absorbed by a divine who goes first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes it first' says A DD takes IT and the lot stands before ION.
explanation.definitionFit: An addition is something extra added on.

clue.text: Traditional at this place and time in the record

parts.note: here means at this place

indicators.note: the abbreviation for time goes inside the record

parts.note: a diary is a daily record

explanation.surface: Customs observed here and now are written down in the log.
explanation.walkthrough: T goes into DIARY to make DITARY.
explanation.definitionFit: Passed down through the generations, as handed-down customs and titles are.

clue.text: Transport in decay: solution must be sustainable

indicators.note: the vehicle is put inside the word for decay

parts.note: rot is decay
a bus is a form of transport

explanation.surface: Fixing crumbling public transport needs a long-lasting answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sturdy and able to withstand strain, so able to be kept going.

clue.text: Holiday pioneer keeps a word (American) for a loosely woven material

indicators.note: the holiday pioneer's name holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: Billy Butlin founded the British holiday camps that bear his name
a term is a word

explanation.surface: A holiday camp founder uses an American word for a flimsy fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: Butlin's holiday camps were a mid-century British institution. TERM and US go inside BUTLIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine open-weave cotton cloth used in cooking for straining.

clue.text: See 20
Scots not at home amid greeting to island state…

indicators.note: the Scots word sits in the middle of the greeting

parts.note: hi is a greeting
awa is Scots for away

explanation.surface: Absent Scots are welcomed to a Pacific island state.
explanation.walkthrough: AWA goes inside HI, and I follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pacific archipelago is the fiftieth of the United States.

clue.text: where there's no pay but love for outstanding girl

parts.note: hon is short for honorary, an unpaid post
love is zero in tennis, O
a lulu is a remarkable person or thing

explanation.surface: An unpaid post but there is love for a remarkable young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: This continues the previous clue: 'where' refers back to the island state, and its capital is the place.
explanation.definitionFit: The state capital of Hawaii is the place meant, following the previous clue's ellipsis.

clue.text: Skidded when about to be unmoveable

indicators.note: the word for skidded goes around the following word

parts.note: slid means skidded

explanation.surface: A car that skidded was about to be stuck fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks attached to 'to' as 'about to', but it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Impassive and unemotional, so not easily stirred.

clue.text: Go into genuine compensation

indicators.note: the word for go is put inside the word for genuine

parts.note: real means genuine
quit means go away

explanation.surface: An instruction to go and seek proper damages.
explanation.definitionFit: Repayment or return for a loss or service is a kind of recompense.

clue.text: Tart embracing recruit used to work for the press

definitions.text: used to work for the press

indicators.note: the word for tart wraps round the word for recruit

parts.note: a flan is an open tart
a tiro is a novice

explanation.surface: A pastry hugging a newcomer used to be news for the papers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the press' suggests newspapers; it is pressing clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: An old iron heated on a stove was used for smoothing clothes.
